title: Job queue
description: The ordered work of one run, at <workspace>/.root-architect/queue/<run_id>.json. This is the deterministic half of the orchestrator: ordering, state and bookkeeping live here so that the agent's attention goes to judging what came back. It is NOT a second record of the work - the envelopes are that, and the queue points at them so every claim here can be checked against the mailbox rather than believed.

run_id.description: Matches the dispatch state's run id, so a queue and the dispatches it produced can be reconciled.

tasks.description: In the order they are to be dispatched. Order is the queue's whole contribution to sequencing: there is no priority field and no scheduler, because a run that needs one has outgrown what root should be handing to a single orchestrator.

name.description: Unique within the run. Feeds envelope filenames and log lines, so it stays shell- and path-safe.

worker.description: Which role this task is for. The orchestrator dispatches it; the queue only records the intent.

brief.description: Path to the brief this task dispatches, relative to the workspace.

state.description: Transitions are monotonic: pending -> dispatched -> returned or failed, and never backwards. A run that could move a task back to pending could rewrite its own history into agreement with a later story, which is the same reason envelopes are append-only.

envelope.description: The envelope that answered this task. Required once the state is returned or failed: a task recorded as answered with nothing to point at is a claim rather than a record, and verify refuses it.
